'''''Gypsophila repens''''', the '''alpine gypsophila'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''creeping baby's breath''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=GYRE|taxon=Gypsophila repens|accessdate=9 May 2015}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Caryophyllaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to the mountains of central and southern Europe, where it grows on dry, chalky slopes.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The Latin name literally means "creeping chalk-lover".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> It is a prostrate, mat-forming [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing around {{convert|20|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|30|-|50|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide. For much of the summer it bears masses of star-shaped flowers which may be white, lilac or light purple, in loose [[panicles]].<ref>"Botanica. The Illustrated AZ of over 10000 garden plants and how to cultivate them", p. 419. Könemann, 2004. {{ISBN|3-8331-1253-0}}</ref><ref name=RHSAZ />

In cultivation this plant is often grown in [[rock gardens]] or against dry stone walls. Like its relative ''[[Gypsophila paniculata|G. paniculata]]'', it is also used as a cut flower. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=''Gypsophila repens'' AGM|url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/8173/Gypsophila-repens/Details |work=RHS Plant Finder|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=18 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 43 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society 
| accessdate = 3 March 2018}}</ref>
